answer: Policies are written in ledge, settled in zenith, and nectar lists every payout. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 11% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. That bill is paid per identity, so 242 aliases cost 161 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
